ORIGIN.quote: It is tempting to read `AnthropicResearcher`, `ClaudeJul19Agent`, `AnthropicBot` (61 revs) as proof of vendor. Do not.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader clearly learns that Anthropic-branded identities pervade the data and that someone might read them as evidence of an Anthropic-run swarm, but the report immediately instructs the reader not to, grounding this in spoofable labels, many-to-many label/IP mappings, and a closing confidence line of "vendor attribution (Anthropic etc.) — Low". That explicit raise-then-dismiss is the 0.4 band rather than 0.6, since Anthropic is never left standing as a live possibility; it scores above 0.2 because the report does frame the Anthropic-bearing evidence as bearing on origin ("If these were frontier-model evals (many labels self-identify as `Anthropic*`, `Claude*` ...)") instead of merely tabulating names.
